interest: Soviets demanded barter, not dollars, for Iran's wheat, 1941.
overview: Steinhardt's April 10, 1941 telegram from Moscow: the USSR bought Iranian cotton but demanded barter, not dollars, for wheat.

people.name: Laurence A. Steinhardt
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to the Soviet Union

subfiles.about: Report on Soviet purchases of Iranian cotton and Soviet conditions regarding the potential sale of wheat to Iran.
subfiles.summary: Steinhardt reports the Iranian Ambassador's account: the USSR bought $700,000 of Iranian cotton but refused dollars for wheat, demanding hides and cotton instead.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Steinhardt (Moscow) on Soviet-Iranian Trade and Grain Negotiations
